title: How to set up an AI receptionist: 6 Key decisions to make
summary: Setting up an AI receptionist takes a few hours to a few weeks, depending on the complexity of your call flows. Learn the key steps to setting up an AI receptionist for any business.
body_markdown:
Wondering how to set up an AI receptionist for your business but feeling overwhelmed or unsure where to start? You’re in the right place.


With most platforms, setting up an AI receptionist is simple. It takes most business owners just a couple of hours. If you need complex call handling, it can take longer. Either way, your success depends on how well you prepare beforehand.


In this article, we’ll walk you through how to prepare, what decisions to make first ** to keep setup simple, how to set it up, and how to tell if it’s working.


##


Is it difficult to set up an AI receptionist?


For most business owners, setting up an AI[virtual receptionist](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-a-virtual-receptionist/) is quick and easy. The difficulty mostly depends on your use case:


Use case Setup time Difficulty


Call forwarding, advanced IVR, voicemail, basic FAQs, and other simple responses 1–2 hours Easy — self-serve


Business hours call routing, scheduling links, and moderate task handling 1–2 days Manageable on your own with webinars or training guides


Multi-job escalation, custom prompt engineering, or end-to-end conversational support 1–2+ weeks Difficult — needs dedicated support


For straightforward answering and information sharing, you can set it up on your own in an hour or two. You don’t need to have prior experience with chatbots or the platform.


More involved AI prompt architecture and conversational AI often take a week or two to build out. A good platform, like Quo, will provide training guides and webinars to support you.


Most business owners can navigate setup on their own, even if it takes a few days.


##


6 Decisions to make before setting up an AI receptionist


Before you set up your[AI receptionist](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/receptionist) — or even choose a platform — you need clarity on six key decisions:


Done Decision What to decide Why it matters


☐ Who gets urgent calls? After-hours path, call routing, on-call schedules Ensures emergencies don’t become voicemails


☐ What should the AI answer? Which questions make up the bulk of your calls, and what easy, repeatable questions can have programmed responses Avoids excessive call transferring for easy requests


☐ What should the AI not handle? How to identify emotional, high-value, or complex calls, and where to route them Reduces frustrated customers and customer churn


☐ What does the AI need to know? What goes in your knowledge base: hours, services, pricing, policies, location, etc. Prevents wrong answers, or constant "I don't know" from the AI


☐ What should the AI connect to? Calendar, CRM, or phone system for third-party AI receptionists Details are recorded and visible to your team


☐ How will you measure if it’s working? KPIs to track, like call abandonment rate or callback rate Catches mistakes before customers do


Let’s break these down.


1. **Who will get urgent calls?**


Every business, from plumbing to dentistry, has urgent calls. Real emergencies should never become voicemails. Align your[after-hours call routing](https://www.quo.com/product/call-routing/business-hours-call-routing) with on-call schedules. Make sure your AI receptionist knows what counts as an urgent call and what number to transfer them to.


1. **What questions can your AI answer first?**


This determines which calls go to your[AI receptionist vs a human receptionist](https://www.quo.com/blog/ai-receptionist-vs-human-receptionist/) . For most businesses, three or four questions make up most of their calls. Often, these are related to operating hours, order or project statuses, or how to book appointments. Easy, repeatable requests are the perfect use of an[automated answering service](https://www.quo.com/blog/automated-answering-service/) .


1. **What should it** ***never*** **answer?**


AI tools shouldn’t handle complex questions, high-value clients, or emotional calls. This leads to frustrated customers and higher churn. Map out issues where the AI should transfer to a human immediately.


1. **What does it need to know?**


Based on the above, what does your AI system need to know? Providing a complete knowledge base makes your AI receptionist as helpful as possible and prevents endless “Sorry, I didn’t quite catch that” loops. These can be things like:


- Operating or store hours
- Locations or locations served
- Available services
- Pricing and availability
- Policies, especially booking, cancellation, or rescheduling policies
- Appointment schedules or order history


Learn more about[setting up a knowledge base in Sona](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/ai-automations/sona/knowledge) .


1. **What should it connect to?**


Connect your AI voice receptionist to your calendar, CRM, and any other necessary platforms. This helps prevent information silos. You can automatically record call details and keep notes visible across your team and tools. If you use third-party AI voice agents, you’ll also need to connect them to your phone system.


1. **How will you measure if it’s working?**


Determine what KPIs you’ll track to make sure your efforts are working. We recommend reporting weekly data. Your Quo dashboard will also track a lot of this for you, so you just need to review it. Track metrics like:


- **Call abandonment rate.** How many customers hang up before completing the task they called about? A high call abandonment rate signals that your AI receptionist isn’t helping customers. You may need to route some calls to humans sooner or improve your AI knowledge base.
- **Callback rate.** What percentage of customers have to call more than once to get their needs met? A high callback rate signals that your AI receptionist isn’t resolving issues accurately on the first try. You may need to improve your knowledge base.
- **CSAT after support calls.** CSAT measures customer satisfaction after an interaction. High CSAT signals that customers are satisfied with the help they received.


You can[connect Claude to Quo](https://www.quo.com/integrations/claude) to surface more insights from Sona-handled calls.


##


How to set up an AI receptionist: Step-by-step


So, how do you set up an AI receptionist? Each platform is different, but we’ll walk you through the basics so you know what to expect.


1. **Name it and pick a voice and tone.** Most platforms offer a handful of AI voices to choose from, with different tone settings. Tone refers to filler phrases, small talk, and personality. Voices refer to the speed, accent, and how the voice sounds.
2. **Fill in your core business information.** This includes things like your business name, hours, and location. Some platforms can generate this information from your website or Google Business Profile. On others, you’ll need to enter it manually.
3. **Set the call-handling rules.** These are decisions #1–#3 from the list above. When is a call urgent? What does it answer, and what are the answers? When it *doesn’t* answer, where does it route the call? In Quo, this is done by adding Sona to your call flow and setting up Sona jobs **.**
4. **Connect it to a number.** Any platform you use requires your AI agent to connect to a working business phone number. Until it’s attached to a number, it can’t answer anything. On some platforms, like Quo, this happens in just a click. On other platforms, you need to forward calls to your AI receptionist.
5. **Connect to the rest of your tech stack.** You can defer this step until you’re sure the basics are working. But at some point, you’ll need to use a webhook, Zapier, or an API to connect your AI receptionist to your other tools. If you have a CRM — like HubSpot or Salesforce — and a calendar system, like Cal.com, start there.
6. **Test, iterate, and publish.** Check whether your AI receptionist platform has a way to do test calls. For example, Quo lets you do mock calls with[Sona](https://www.quo.com/sona) to test configuration and responses. That’s a better option than burning through allocated calls or minutes. But if not, call several times to test all your options. Adjust your job configuration and knowledge base until you get consistent correct responses. Then let your AI receptionist start answering live calls.


Getting started with Sona is easy: use these step-by-step[Sona setup instructions](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/ai-automations/sona/overview) to get started with the basics quickly


##


What to do in the first two weeks


An AI receptionist should make your job a *lot* easier, but it’s not a set-it-and-forget-it tool. Here’s what to do in the first two weeks to make sure it’s as effective as possible.


**1. Listen to the first calls and read the transcripts.** QA for the first calls is crucial to make sure your AI receptionist is responding how you’d like. Listen to the call recordings, read the transcripts, and look out for any of these five things:


- Questions it couldn’t answer
- Times it responded inaccurately or didn’t take the correct action
- Callers repeating themselves
- Callers hanging up
- Edge cases you didn’t consider


**2. Add questions it couldn’t answer to the knowledge base.** Sometimes these are simple answers the AI can respond to in the future. For others, you may need to add new instructions.


**3. Re-route or adjust the configuration for caller frustration.** If callers repeat themselves or hang up, your AI agent likely needs more information. In some cases, you may need clearer actions or to transfer a call sooner. Identify the best option, then adjust the configuration.


**4. Make sure all transfers reached someone.** If the AI transferred an emergency after-hours call, did it reach the right team member or go to voicemail? Did any transferred calls get dropped? Could call routing settings be improved?


**5. Update your AI knowledge base anytime your hours, pricing, or services change.** Keeping your AI phone agents accurate and up to date is key to making sure they work effectively for you. That way, your customers get the right information the first time.


##


Verdict


AI receptionists can help local businesses improve lead qualification, reduce hold queues, and free up your team. Setting up an AI receptionist is relatively straightforward. The key to making it simple: do the behind-the-scenes prep work first.


The “measure twice, cut once” rule applies here. Once you have the basics, configuring more complex call routing for your AI receptionist will be easier.


Take an hour or two in the first few weeks to read the transcripts and iterate on your configuration. Fixing gaps early can help you get the most from your AI receptionist.


**So, ready to get started?**


If you already pay for a business phone system, start there before adding a second vendor. For example, every Quo workspace includes 10 free Sona calls each month so you can test the system before you commit.[Try Quo and Sona with a seven-day free trial](https://my.quo.com/signup) .

##


FAQs


**Can I build my own AI receptionist?**


Yes, you can. To do so, you’ll need to configure and connect four main pieces:


1. Telephony to receive and route the call
2. A speech-to-text tool to turn what the caller says into text
3. An LLM with natural language processing to work out intent and generate the reply
4. A TTS — text-to-speech — tool to turn that reply back into voice


Building your own AI receptionist using tools like ChatGPT and ElevenLabs usually takes 20–30 hours for the initial setup. Plan to spend a couple of hours each week on continued maintenance and updates. Typically, this is only worth it if the receptionist is the product you’re selling or you have a call flow no platform supports.


If you just need your phone answered, use a platform with an AI receptionist, like Quo. It’s much easier and faster.


**Do I need technical skills to create an AI receptionist?**


It depends. For simple setups and call flows with an AI receptionist on a business phone platform, you need very little technical ability. If you’re DIYing or building a more complicated flow with custom prompting, you’ll need more technical skills to lean on. The level of technical skills needed generally comes down to:


– Your setup
– The platform you use
– Your use case and call flow complexity
– If you’re building vs buying


**How long does it take to set up an AI receptionist?**


It can take anywhere from a few hours to a few days. If you’re setting up a simple call answering or routing system, plan for a few hours. If you need a more complicated call flow — like custom prompts for appointment booking and multiple platform connections — plan for several days. Edge cases can take several weeks.


**How much does a virtual receptionist cost?**


Human virtual receptionist services range from $250–$2,000+ per month.[Virtual receptionist costs](https://www.quo.com/blog/virtual-receptionist-cost/) typically vary based on provider, use case, and minutes used. AI receptionists range from $25–$300+ per month. For example, Quo includes 10 free Sona calls a month on every plan, then charges $25 for around 40 calls and up to $199 for 600 calls.


**What happens when the AI receptionist can’t answer?**


Typically, the easiest solution is to have the AI receptionist route the call to a live team member. Other options include scheduling a callback, taking a message or directing the customer to where to find help, like your website.


Learn more about[what an AI receptionist can do](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-ai-receptionist/) .


**Are AI receptionists secure?**


AI receptionist security varies by provider. Ask potential providers what happens to call recordings and transcripts. Be sure to check the level of security they offer. Look for platforms that are GDPR and HIPAA compliant.
